clips.send: Common mix-up: Mutations are random. The moth cannot choose to mutate into a useful color.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Mutations are random. The moth cannot choose to mutate into a useful color.

clips.send: Common mix-up: The moths did not turn dark because soot stained them or because they “wanted” camouflage. Dark moths already existed (from a gene mutation); they simply survived and had more offspring on dark bark. Individuals do not evolve; populations do.

clips.send: Light peppered moth. Camouflaged on pale bark. White wings with black “pepper” speckles. Nearly all peppered moths were light-colored before the Industrial Revolution. On dark, sooty bark it stands out, and birds find it easily.

clips.send: Tree bark (environment). Decides which colors are hidden. Moths rest on tree trunks during the day, where birds hunt them. Before factories, English tree trunks were pale. Coal smoke in the 1800s darkened them with soot. Use the Bark color slider: the environment changes, so the “best” moth color changes too.

clips.send: Dark peppered moth. Camouflaged on sooty bark. The dark form comes from a mutation in one gene, and it is inherited. The first dark moth was recorded near Manchester, England in 1848. By 1895 about 98 percent of moths there were dark. It did not appear BECAUSE of the soot; it already existed and was favored by selection.

clips.send: Radius and ulna. Two forearm bones. Two bones side by side in the forearm. In the bat the radius is long and the ulna is tiny; in the whale both are short and flat.
clips.text: Radius & ulna. Two forearm bones. Two bones side by side in the forearm.. In the bat the radius is long and the ulna is tiny; in the whale both are short and flat.

clips.send: Humerus. One upper-arm bone. Every limb here has ONE bone from the shoulder to the elbow. It is short and thick in the whale, long in the human.

clips.send: Carpals. Wrist bones. A cluster of small bones that form the wrist. They let the hand or paw bend.
clips.text: Carpals. Wrist bones. A cluster of small bones that form the wrist.. They let the hand or paw bend.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Homologous is not equal to same job. A bat wing and a butterfly wing do the same job but are built differently: they are analogous, not homologous.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Homologous ≠ same job. A bat wing and a butterfly wing do the same job but are built differently: they are analogous, not homologous.

clips.send: Lichen and soot. A change in the environment. Pale lichens grow on trees where the air is clean. Air pollution killed the lichens and coated bark in black soot, so dark moths became better hidden. After clean-air laws (1956 in Britain), lichens returned and light moths became common again.

clips.send: Metacarpals. Palm bones. Five long bones in the palm. In the bat they are stretched very long to hold up the wing.

clips.send: Phalanges. Finger bones. The bones of the fingers (or toes). Whale flippers have extra phalanges; cats walk on theirs.

clips.send: 浅色桦尺蛾。在浅色树皮上很隐蔽。白色的翅膀上有黑色的“胡椒”斑点。工业革命以前，几乎所有的桦尺蛾都是浅色的。在被烟尘熏黑的树皮上，它非常显眼，很容易被鸟发现。

clips.send: 腕骨。手腕的骨头。组成手腕的一组小骨头。让手或爪能够弯曲。

clips.send: 深色桦尺蛾。在被熏黑的树皮上很隐蔽。深色类型来自一个基因的突变，并且可以遗传。1848 年在英国曼彻斯特附近首次记录到深色蛾子；到 1895 年，那里约 百分之98 的蛾子都是深色的。它并不是“因为”烟尘才出现的；它早已存在，只是被自然选择保留了下来。

clips.send: 树皮（环境）。决定哪种颜色更隐蔽。蛾子白天停在树干上休息，鸟就在树干上捕食它们。工厂出现以前，英国的树干颜色很浅。19 世纪燃煤产生的烟尘把树干熏黑了。拖动“树皮颜色”滑块：环境变了，“最好”的蛾子颜色也随之改变。

clips.send: 地衣与烟尘。环境的变化。在空气清新的地方，树上长满浅色的地衣。空气污染杀死了地衣，并在树皮上覆盖了黑色烟尘，深色蛾子因此更隐蔽。英国 1956 年通过《清洁空气法》后，地衣又长了回来，浅色蛾子重新变得常见。

clips.send: 掌骨。手掌的骨头。手掌中的五根长骨。蝙蝠的掌骨被拉得很长，用来撑起翅膀。

clips.send: 桡骨和尺骨。两根前臂骨。前臂中并排的两根骨头。蝙蝠的桡骨很长、尺骨很小；鲸的桡骨和尺骨都又短又扁。
